intro: Spanish words that look like English words and mean something else.
p.embarazada.consejo: «Embarazada» is not «embarrassed». To feel embarrassed you say «avergonzado».
p.actualmente.consejo: It means «now», not «actually». For «actually» you say «en realidad».
p.sensible.consejo: It is «sensitive». For English «sensible» (of good judgement) you say «sensato».
p.constipado.consejo: In Spain, «estar constipado» means having a cold. English «constipated» is something else.
p.carpeta.consejo: It is a «folder», not a «carpet». The floor covering is called «alfombra» or «moqueta».
p.librería.consejo: It is not «library». To borrow books you go to the «biblioteca».
p.éxito.consejo: It is «success», not «exit». The way out of a place is called «salida».
p.asistir a.consejo: You say «asistir a una reunión». For «to assist» you say «ayudar».
p.realizar.consejo: It is «to carry out». For «to realise» you say «darse cuenta de».
p.soportar.consejo: It means «to put up with». For «to support» you say «apoyar».
p.pretender.consejo: It is «to intend». For «to pretend» you say «fingir».
p.largo.consejo: It is «long», not «large». For «large» you say «grande».
p.discutir.consejo: In everyday use it is «to argue». To chat about a topic you say «hablar de».
p.parientes.consejo: They are «relatives», not «parents». Parents are called «padres».
b1.texto:
Thousands of Spanish and English words are true cousins: **importante**, **posible**, **universidad**. A few dozen are traps, and they are very common words.

Some are embarrassing: **embarazada** is «pregnant» and **constipado** is «having a cold».

Some quietly change your meaning: **actualmente** is «currently», **eventualmente** is «possibly», **largo** is «long», **sensible** is «sensitive».

Some are verbs you will use every day: **asistir a** (to attend), **realizar** (to carry out), **soportar** (to put up with), **pretender** (to intend), **discutir** (to argue), **recordar** (to remember, not «to record»), **contestar** (to answer).

And some are nouns: **la librería**, **la carpeta**, **el éxito**, **la noticia** (a piece of news), **los parientes**, **la decepción** (disappointment), **el compromiso** (commitment).
b2.f0.texto: I have a cold and I cannot attend the meeting.
b2.f1.texto: Have you been to the bookshop to buy a folder?
b2.f2.texto: At the moment I go out very little.
b2.f3.texto: My sister is pregnant and very sensitive these days.
b2.f4.texto: I am very happy for her.
b2.f5.texto: Her latest book was a huge success.
b2.f6.texto: Does she put up well with long interviews?
b2.f7.texto: Her relatives look after her without arguing.
b4.texto:
Learn each pair whole: what it **does** mean and what it does **not**.

- **embarazada** = pregnant (not «embarrassed»: avergonzado)
- **actualmente** = currently (not «actually»: en realidad)
- **sensible** = sensitive (not «sensible»: sensato)
- **librería** = bookshop (not «library»: biblioteca)
- **éxito** = success (not «exit»: salida)
- **asistir a** = to attend (not «to assist»: ayudar)
- **realizar** = to carry out (not «to realise»: darse cuenta)
- **soportar** = to put up with (not «to support»: apoyar)
- **pretender** = to intend (not «to pretend»: fingir)
- **largo** = long (not «large»: grande)
- **discutir** = to argue (not «to discuss»: hablar de)
- **parientes** = relatives (not «parents»: padres)

Watch the prepositions: **asistir a** a meeting, **soportar** the noise (no preposition).
b4.e0.texto: I currently work in a bookshop downtown.
b4.e1.texto: I intend to carry out my project before June.
b5.f0.texto: The bookshop on the square smells of old paper and wood.
b5.f1.texto: In the window rests a green folder next to a pile of notebooks.
b5.f2.texto: A book with blue covers awaits its success on the central table.
b5.f3.texto: The readers walk along the long aisles with slow steps.
b5.f4.texto: Behind the counter, a woman smiles with her head tilted.
b5.f5.texto: A foreign tourist comes in with a red nose and tired eyes.
b5.f6.texto: She asks about the library in a soft voice.
b5.f7.texto: The bookseller listens to her patiently and points out the street opposite.
b5.f8.texto: Outside the fine rain draws circles in the puddles.
b5.f9.texto: The tourist leaves, grateful, towards the library across the street.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That is «avergonzada»: it is the false friend.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Embarazada» only means she is expecting a baby.
b6.pregunta: What does «Mi hermana está embarazada» mean?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done: it means «at this moment».
b7.o1.refuerzo: It means «a long time ago», the opposite.
b7.pregunta: I want to say «currently». Which word is missing?
b8.o0.refuerzo: There you buy them. They are not lent.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That is it: the library lends books for free.
b8.o2.refuerzo: A carpeta is for keeping papers.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Un suceso is something that happens, an incident.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Una salida is the way you leave a place.
b9.pregunta: I want to say «success». Which word is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Realizar» is to do or carry out, not to realise.
b10.o1: Me di cuenta de que llegaba tarde
b10.o1.refuerzo: Well done: «darse cuenta de» is «to realise».
b10.pregunta: How do you say «I realised I was late»?
b11.o0.refuerzo: Well done: «soportar» is to put up with something annoying.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Apoyar» is «to support», to give someone help.
b11.o2.refuerzo: «Asistir» is to be present at an event.
b11.pregunta: I want to say «I can't stand the noise».
b12.frase: Actualmente no salgo mucho de casa
b12.traduccion: At the moment I do not go out much
p.constipada.consejo: Common in Spain for a bad cold. The stress falls on «PA» and the feminine ending «-da» shows a woman.
p.soporta.consejo: From «soportar», to bear. Think of a pillar that supports weight: the root is «porte».
p.entrevistas.consejo: Plural of «entrevista». The «v» sounds like «b», so it is «en-tre-BIS-tas».
p.cuidan.consejo: From «cuidado», care. The «ui» is read as «wi», so the word starts with a «kw» sound.
p.pretendo.consejo: From «pretender», to intend or aim for. The «e» before «nd» keeps its sound.
p.asistieron.consejo: From «asistir», to attend. The «ie» forms a diphthong: «TYE».
p.tapas.consejo: Here it means the covers of a book. In Spain «tapas» also means small snacks served with drinks.
p.central.consejo: The «c» before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain. The stress falls on «TRAL» at the end.
p.recorren.consejo: From «correr», to run, with «re-» meaning through or across. The «rr» in the middle is strong.
p.pasillos.consejo: Plural of «pasillo». The «ll» sounds like a «y» in most of Spain.
p.inclinada.consejo: From «inclinar», to tilt. The feminine «-a» agrees with «la cabeza», which is feminine.
p.extranjera.consejo: The «j» sounds like an English «h», so the stress is on «HE»: «eks-tran-HE-ra».
p.librera.consejo: From «libro», book. The ending «-era» names the person who works with that thing.
p.agradecida.consejo: From «agradecer», to thank. The «c» sounds like «th» here, so «-thi-da».
p.llegaba.consejo: From «llegar», to arrive. The «ll» sounds like «y» here, and the «-aba» ending is the past tense.
p.soporto.consejo: From «soportar», to bear. The stress falls on «POR», the second syllable.
